beats.headline: The deal for the Gate
beats.text: I arrive, I introduce myself as my client's counsel, and we proceed to terms. The Gate goes back. Temporarily. In consideration: four mercenaries at no charge to my client, Bomo, the Sledge, Clay-ton and Very Sullen, and two spells for Bomo and the Sledge that reproduce two of the Gate's abilities, teleport to stairwell and zerzura. My client wanted to keep it. Everyone wants to keep it. A negotiation is what you get instead.

beats.headline: Say nothing, touch nothing
beats.text: First instruction to my client. Any time he gets hauled in front of one of these liaisons, he says nothing except that he wants to talk to his lawyer, and he doesn't touch anything until I get there. They were trying to get him to pick up the artifact while it was under administrative hold, which would have deleted the item. I am his attorney. Nobody else's. Not the cat, not the lady who turned into a shovel. What I get out of it is credits. Not a lot. Not too many outfits hire a Null.

beats.headline: Subsection 674
beats.text: Second request. The sixth floor is where secondary programs go to die, and a limited number get licences to continue. We want one for Sensation Entertainment's Vengeance of the Daughter. Not possible, says the liaison: licences are an AI decision, at the end of the floor, by lottery. Subsection 674, paragraph five or six of the secondary program amendment, buddy-boy. Showrunners running below expected profits may give emergency use to a single program. The price is an extra twenty percent to Borant. They've already agreed, I tell them, and wave my device. They haven't. I couldn't reach them.

beats.headline: A court order to write
beats.text: I now need a court order to send my client a message; he can still send me all he likes. His complaints about hunters getting outside information have caused a stir. Sensation has agreed to Borant's offer of a ninth-floor extension but wants a few days before signing. My read: make the program more exciting without the spotlight throwing the star into the shadow. Too bright, and they might pull his plug. The other matter is one hundred fifty million credits. His net worth out here is about 117, against a tax bill of maybe 50. I have an idea. I'm working on it.

beats.headline: Zerzura, and the fine print
beats.text: Fifteen days back, I lay out the spell for my client. Zerzura moves a whole town, buildings and NPCs, one floor down. Terms: cast only at the end of a floor, one attempt, five minutes to cast, so we install it in a mercenary. The town lands at random, which means the worst place available, and everything it kills rises as a revenant that hunts the villagers and the caster until they are all dead. On these levels it skips floors. Remex learned that. Everybody will want you to do it. Everybody likes carnage when it's not them.

beats.headline: A briefing under the liaison's nose
beats.text: While the cat calls out screencap numbers, I brief my client, fast, because there is only so much I can legally say with that goat standing there. His castle landed on the Lemig Sortion's battlefield and splattered half their army. The Lemigs are squatting in the wreck, and their commander is still stuck in the Desperado Club. They filed a grievance calling the landing an attack; we argued it was an AI action, successfully. Tina is still an allosaurus. The changelings have started building his stronghold. Ferdinand lost his hat and moved to the city. I petitioned to attend his preproduction meeting. Denied.

beats.headline: Settled caselaw, and a trade
beats.text: I arrive, and they have been talking without me. The liaison wants my client's plastic bin. My position: settled caselaw, Grixist Swarm v. Syndicate Council. Legal sponsor box, loot on the playing field, already in inventory; he has no standing. His position: Valtay enhancement pills and a communicator are not permitted as found loot. My client offers to trade. I tell him to be quiet and propose a trade. The deal is done, and I am removed in the middle of a sentence.

beats.headline: A recap for a school report
beats.text: My niece Tempest needs a recap of my client's eighth floor for school. Terms: she fixes my sink. The recap: my client killed Quan Ch for his key. The dog girl with the flamethrower died, and he now has the flamethrower and the pet. On the ninth, neither Donut nor Katia can leave until every naga is dead, and even then only one of them can. With the recorder off, she asks whether representing him puts me in danger. I tell her the truth. I think we all are.

beats.headline: Straight off the rack
beats.text: Formalities. I'm volunteered this season: three exit negotiations, and my client is the last of them. The other two took deals. Neither is his inner circle. His deals are all shit, a side effect of so many survivors: fifty seasons undead; the Desperado Club bomber's guild, with a contingent exit clause. The last isn't bad. Chaco's last season, a replacement wanted, offered jointly to Carl and Donut and still open at the end of the next floor. Telling him about that floor adds a season to any deal. He consents. Vehicles, point A to point B, and last place loses its containment.

beats.headline: A contract on his family
beats.text: A tie on, a booth free, and my niece on my tablet with blood on her temple. Taurins at my brother's house, on a contract taken with my client's wife. Two of them die on camera; Tempest has the blaster I gave her. I retain Kiki for one credit, for legal help and the other kind. Princess Chandra has been filing into the void since Donut put a hit on her. Now she has sent people to my family. Terms to follow.

beats.headline: One deal, and a warning
beats.text: Three minutes with my client. One deal on offer: a single season of indenture, then freedom. I show him the paperwork. I tell him I would not trust it, and that I would understand if he took it. No exit is offered at the close of the eleventh; one is offered at the start of the twelfth, and I would not trust that either. He declines. I leave. I do not tell him why I am in a hurry.
